title: Brisbane Airport Curfew and Demand Management Bill 2022
short_title: Brisbane Airport Curfew and Demand Management Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would impose a night curfew and hourly movement limit at Brisbane Airport, supported by slot allocation, compliance monitoring and long-term operating arrangements.
The curfew would run from 10 pm to 6 am Queensland time, and aircraft movements would be capped at 45 in each regulated hour.
Emergency and exceptional circumstance arrangements would qualify the restrictions, while a long-term operating plan would address aircraft noise and community impacts following broad consultation.
changes: The minister could lower the hourly movement limit after consulting industry and community stakeholders.
A Slot Manager would develop and administer a scheme allocating permissions for gate movements.
A Compliance Committee would develop a scheme to monitor authorised gate movements and infringements.
Airservices Australia would monitor aircraft movements and report compliance with the movement limit to the minister.
summary.affected: Aircraft operators, nearby residents, Airservices Australia and the proposed airport management bodies would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Adam Paul Bandt
speeches.brief: The Brisbane Airport Curfew and Demand Management Bill 2022 proposes a 10 pm to 6 am curfew, a cap of 45 flights per hour, and a long‑term operating plan to reduce aircraft noise over Brisbane, citing a survey where 81% of residents reported sleep disruption and 68% suffered mental distress. The bill follows community campaigning by the Brisbane Flight Path Community Alliance, Greens candidates Max Chandler‑Mather and Stephen Bates, and aims to force the minister to shift more flights over Moreton Bay and distribute traffic fairly.
